papers.title: High-Fidelity Baseline Design and Station Keeping Analyses for Earth-Moon Vertical Orbits
papers.summary: Earth-Moon vertical orbits are periodic solutions of the circular restricted three-body problem (CR3BP) with substantial out-of-plane motion, considered for high-latitude lunar observation and cislunar navigation. This work develops an end-to-end framework for high-fidelity reference generation under rotating-frame geometry constraints and receding-horizon model predictive control. A representative $L_2$ vertical orbit yields a 5.5-year reference with negligible deterministic correction and remains maintainable in five-year Monte Carlo simulations under realistic uncertainties. The workflow produces locally optimal solutions across 90 consecutive daily start epochs and 200 catalog cases. Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponent along the reference and stable/unstable CR3BP directions interpret station-keeping behavior.
papers.title_ja: 地球-月垂直軌道の高忠実度ベースライン設計とステーションキーピング解析
papers.summary_ja: 円形制限三体問題（CR3BP）における地球-月垂直軌道に対し、回転座標系の幾何学的制約下で高忠実度な参照軌道を生成するエンドツーエンドのフレームワークを提案する。再帰地平線モデル予測制御（MPC）を用いることで、L2点の垂直軌道において5.5年間の参照軌道が決定論的補正をほぼ必要とせず、現実的な不確実性下でも5年間のモンテカルロシミュレーションで維持可能であることを示した。さらに、90日連続の開始エポックと200件のカタログケースに対して局所最適解を生成し、有限時間ライプノフ指数を用いてステーションキーピングの挙動を解釈した。

papers.title: Deflating the Hessian: Rank-4 W4A4 Quantization for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
papers.summary: In diffusion transformers, low-rank branches can mitigate 4-bit weight--activation (W4A4) post-training quantization (PTQ) loss by decomposing each weight into a low-bit residual and a high-precision low-rank component. Existing low-rank PTQ approaches, however, either optimize low-rank compensation and residual quantization separately, often requiring higher ranks, or rely on second-order weight updates without explicitly modeling activation quantization error, which becomes particularly pronounced under 4-bit quantization. To address these limitations, we present \method{}, a unified framework modeling low-rank-assisted W4A4 PTQ as a coupled calibration problem and deriving optimization-based solvers from the joint objective. Eliminating the output-side low-rank factor yields a \emph{deflated Hessian} that discounts residual errors already captured by the low-rank component, while an activation-noise surrogate is incorporated to suppress activation quantization error. Across five diffusion backbones, rank-4 \method{} consistently outperforms rank-4 SVDQuant in PSNR and LPIPS. It further surpasses rank-32 SVDQuant on SANA-1.6B, FLUX.1-schnell, and FLUX.1-dev with an $8\times$ smaller rank and up to $6.25\times$ faster quantization. Furthermore, on the Qwen3-8B LLM, rank-4 \method{} improves MMLU accuracy from 61.50\% to 68.17\% over rank-32 SVDQuant. Overall, \method{} achieves better W4A4 performance with substantially lower rank and quantization cost.
papers.title_ja: ヘッセ行列の縮小：マルチモーダル拡散トランスフォーマー向けランク4 W4A4量子化
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、拡散トランスフォーマーにおける4bit重み・活性化（W4A4）量子化の精度劣化を低ランク補償で緩和する統一フレームワークを提案する。低ランク成分と残差量子化を結合した較正問題として定式化し、ヘッセ行列の縮小と活性化ノイズのサロゲートモデルを用いた最適化手法を導出する。既存手法と比較し、ランク4でSVDQuantのランク32を上回るPSNR/LPIPS性能を実現し、量子化コストを最大6.25倍高速化した。さらにQwen3-8B LLMにおいてもMMLU精度を大幅に向上させ、LLMと拡散モデル双方で有効性を示した。

papers.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
papers.summary: Do LLM scientific agents rely only on their initial task context, or do they adapt their decisions in response to experimental feedback? We study this question in neural operator adaptation, where a large language model (LLM) selects fine-tuning configurations under a limited trial budget. Across transfers within and between partial differential equation (PDE) families, the LLM achieves lower held-out test nRMSE than random search and Bayesian optimisation in nearly every matched comparison. Endpoint performance alone cannot distinguish what happens, so we verify each attribution with controlled interventions. Before observing any validation score, the LLM's first configuration already ranks near the top of the corresponding random-search pool, indicating a useful initial bias. A complementary cold-start intervention shows that the selected base learning rate shifts with the PDE description. Once feedback becomes available, reassigning validation scores among evaluated configurations changes the next proposal in every case tested, whereas a value-preserving rewrite produces no comparable aggregate effect. These interventions establish that the LLM's decision-level actions respond to the given task and observed outcomes, showing that it combines a task-dependent prior with sensitivity to experimental feedback.
papers.title_ja: 事前知識かフィードバックか？ニューラルオペレータ適応におけるLLMの行動分析
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、LLMがニューラルオペレータのファインチューニング設定を選択する際、初期のタスク文脈（事前知識）と実験フィードバックのどちらに依存するかを調査した。PDE間の転移において、LLMはランダムサーチやベイズ最適化を上回る性能を示した。介入実験により、LLMはタスク依存の事前バイアスを持ちつつ、検証スコアなどのフィードバックにも敏感に反応して次の提案を変更することが確認された。

papers.title: Exact SO(3)-Equivariant Isotropic Kernels for Rotation-Robust Neural Dynamics
papers.summary: Neural surrogates for vector-valued partial differential equations can fit training data yet change their predictions when the same physical state is expressed in a rotated coordinate frame. We study this failure on three-dimensional Navier--Stokes dynamics observed at irregularly placed points. We introduce the Invariant-Conditioned Isotropic Kernel Neural Operator (IKNO), a compact graph model that builds local interactions from scalar quantities unchanged by rotation and vector directions that rotate with the data. Consequently, rotating the positions and velocities rotates the predicted velocity change in exactly the same way. On a held-out test set fixed after model design, training unconstrained graph models on randomly rotated examples reduces but does not eliminate their coordinate dependence. In contrast, IKNO is consistent to numerical precision, matches the forecasting accuracy of a general rotation-aware Tensor Field Network with $5.6$ times fewer parameters, and outperforms a parameter-matched graph simulator. These results show that a compact, PDE-specialized model can remove coordinate dependence without sacrificing forecasting accuracy.
papers.title_ja: 回転ロバストなニューラルダイナミクスのための厳密なSO(3)等変等方性カーネル
papers.summary_ja: ベクトル値偏微分方程式（Navier-Stokes）のサロゲートモデルにおいて、座標系回転による予測の不一致を解決するIKNO（Invariant-Conditioned Isotropic Kernel Neural Operator）を提案する。回転不変なスカラー量とデータと共に回転するベクトル方向から局所相互作用を構築し、座標系の変化に対して厳密に等変性を保つ。パラメータ数がTensor Field Networkの約1/5.6倍とコンパクトでありながら、同等以上の予測精度を実現し、座標依存性を数値精度レベルで除去した。

papers.title: F$^3$NO: Frequency-Decomposed Finite-Time Flow-map Neural Operators with Cross-Scale Conditioning
papers.summary: Neural operators enable fast PDE forecasting, but repeated predictions accumulate errors and fine-scale structures remain difficult to resolve. We introduce a frequency-decomposed finite-time flow-map neural operator (F$^3$NO) that leverages updated low-frequency features to guide nonlinear refinement of high-frequency information. Within each layer, this cross-scale conditioning connects global spectral processing with local detail refinement. The model directly predicts states at specified future times and adjusts the contributions of the two branches according to the prediction interval. For longer trajectories, it combines parallel predictions within short temporal segments with recursive propagation between segments. Experiments on five PDE benchmarks demonstrate improved forecasting accuracy over autoregressive and direct-prediction baselines. Ablations show that frequency-decomposed refinement can improve accuracy with fewer parameters, while the benefits of segmentation depend on spatial resolution and dynamical regime.
papers.title_ja: F^3NO: 周波数分解有限時間フローマップニューラルオペレータとクロススケール条件付け
papers.summary_ja: ニューラルオペレータによるPDE予測における誤差蓄積と高周波数構造の解像度問題を解決するため、周波数分解有限時間フローマップニューラルオペレータ（F^3NO）を提案する。低周波数特徴量を用いて高周波数情報の非線形精緻化を導くクロススケール条件付けを導入し、指定された未来時刻の状態を直接予測する。長期的な予測では、短い時間区間内の並列予測と区間間の再帰的伝播を組み合わせることで安定性を確保する。5つのPDEベンチマークにおいて、自己回帰型および直接予測型のベースラインと比較して予測精度が向上し、パラメータ数を減らしつつ精度を維持できることが示された。

papers.title: Numerical Neural Operator: Connection Between Numerical Analysis and the Operator Learning and Building Discretized Neural Operators from Finite Element Methods
papers.summary: Operator learning aims to learn mappings between function spaces and has been widely used for PDE-related problems. This raises two fundamental questions. First, is there a connection between standard numerical methods and neural operators, given that both are designed to approximate PDE solution operators? Second, when a neural operator is trained on numerically generated data, does it approximate the underlying infinite dimension operator, the training data themselves, or the discretized numerical scheme used to generate them? A key hypothesis in the paper is that the trained neural operator may mimic the discretized numerical schemes that generate the training data. The hypothesis has been partially and preliminary verified by the linear approximation principle proposed in Chen Chen 1995 paper and the following scaling law papers. However, neural operator approximation from the perspective of numerical discretization remains unexplored. In this work, we consider a class of PDEs and derive neural operator architectures from the numerical schemes. Firstly, the numerical basis functions, such as finite element basis functions, can be approximated or directly constructed by learnable neural networks. Then the finite difference schemes for temporal discretization can be unrolled into iterative neural architectures that generate the coefficients of the basis of the resulting neural operator. By leveraging numerical analysis, we establish convergence error estimates for these numerically derived neural operators. Notably, the network size depends polynomial on the approximation error in $L_2$, improving the nested exponential dependence derived in the general neural operator approximation and aligning with the numerical observations. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate reduced errors and improved parameter efficiency.
papers.title_ja: 数値ニューラルオペレータ：数値解析とオペレータ学習の接続、および有限要素法からの離散化ニューラルオペレータの構築
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、偏微分方程式（PDE）の解を近似する数値手法とニューラルオペレータ間の理論的接続を確立する。有限要素法の基底関数や時間離散化スキームをニューラルネットワークで表現し、数値解析に基づいた収束誤差推定を導出する。従来の汎用ニューラルオペレータとは異なり、ネットワークサイズが誤差に対して多項式依存性を示すことを証明し、パラメータ効率の向上を実証した。

papers.title: Uncovering and Fixing Collider Bias in Bayesian PINNs
papers.summary: Bayesian physics-informed neural networks (B-PINNs) are a popular framework for parameter and state inference from sparse or noisy observations. They are commonly formulated via a collider structure, in which physical and trajectory parameters are assumed to be a priori independent and become coupled through virtual likelihoods on differential-equation residuals that enforce physical consistency. We show that this modeling choice can induce severe systematic bias in the posterior over physical parameters: even when the prior is favorably centered on the ground-truth parameters, the resulting posterior can drift away and concentrate far from them. As a remedy, we advocate a hierarchical chain model in which physics generates trajectories, which in turn generate observations. The chain model does not suffer from this posterior bias, but it poses a harder, so-called doubly intractable, inference problem due to a physics-dependent normalization constant. This challenge can be resolved by discretizing the underlying stochastic dynamics, after which the chain posterior can be sampled exactly with particle MCMC. We identify two distinct mechanisms characterizing the collider bias, derive analytical approximations of their magnitudes, and establish diagnostic criteria for predicting when standard B-PINNs remain reliable. Experiments confirm the predicted bias and show that the chain formulation successfully avoids it.
papers.title_ja: ベイズ物理情報ニューラルネットにおけるコライダーバイアスの発見と修正
papers.summary_ja: ベイズ物理情報ニューラルネット（B-PINN）の標準的なコライダー構造が、物理パラメータの事後分布に重大な系統的バイアスをもたらすことを示した。このバイアスは事前分布が真値に近くても発生し、推論精度を損なう。解決策として、物理が軌跡を生成し、それが観測を生む階層的チェーンモデルを提案した。このモデルは粒子MCMCを用いることで、困難な推論問題を解決しつつバイアスを回避できることを実験で確認した。

papers.title: Ghost tasking for parametrized Gaussian Processes solving linear differential equations
papers.summary: Physics-informed machine learning has gained significant attention in recent years. In regimes of limited data, parametrized Gaussian processes have become popular. Existing approaches, however, often face limitations, such as requiring parametrizable (also called controllable) systems or a large number of output tasks. In this work, we introduce a systematic procedure we call "ghost tasking", using auxiliary tasks to circumvent these limitations. We prove that such ghost tasks can render any non-parametrizable system effectively parametrizable, enabling algorithmic construction of parametrized Gaussian Processes while keeping the number of required tasks (i.e. output dimensions) and latent functions low. We find that ghost tasking performs especially well in an inverse problem setting, even with very few available data. We show the usage and power of ghost tasking in three experiments, providing systematic comparisons to the only other currently available method applicable to all experiments. We provide necessary syntax and explications for two computer algebra programs that compute parametrizations for systems with polynomial or rational coefficients. Our theoretical results extend to systems with meromorphic functions.
papers.title_ja: 線形微分方程式を解くパラメトリックガウス過程におけるゴーストタスク法
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、データが限られた環境下で線形微分方程式を解くためのパラメトリックガウス過程（PGP）の手法を提案する。既存手法が直面する「系がパラメトリック（制御可能）である必要がある」「出力タスク数が多すぎる」という制約を、補助的な「ゴーストタスク」を導入することで回避する。理論的に、この手法により非パラメトリックな系も実質的にパラメトリック化でき、必要なタスク数と潜在関数を低く保ちつつアルゴリズム的にPGPを構築できることを証明した。逆問題設定において非常に少ないデータでも高性能を発揮し、多項式や有理関数係数を持つ系のパラメトリゼーション計算のためのコンピュータ代数プログラムとの連携も示している。

papers.title: Exploiting Gradients in Bayesian Inference of Expensive Simulators
papers.summary: Simulators based on differential equations are ubiquitous in science and engineering. They are often used in simulation-based inference to evaluate the posterior distribution of the input parameters based on real-world observations of the simulator outputs. However, inference becomes challenging when individual simulator evaluations are computationally expensive. In such cases, a Bayesian optimization-based active learning approach with Gaussian process surrogate models has been used to maximize the information obtained from a limited simulation budget. Recently, gradients of simulator outputs with respect to input parameters have become increasingly available, yet they are rarely exploited for inference. Even though we only need to learn the simulator input-output relationship, gradient information can provide an additional valuable signal to guide the active learning procedure. This is of particular interest in the case of expensive simulators, when sample efficiency is crucial. In this paper, we demonstrate how incorporating gradient information into the Gaussian process surrogate accelerates Bayesian optimization-based inference under a limited simulation budget. Our results show significant improvement in convergence speed from using gradient information. For reverse-mode differentiation, the inference efficiency gains are maintained when accounting for the additional computational cost. In contrast, for forward-mode differentiation, the inference speed-up does not outweigh the computational costs. These results indicate that gradient-enhanced surrogates are beneficial primarily in problems where the number of parameters exceeds the output dimensionality, where reverse-mode differentiation is efficient.
papers.title_ja: 高コストシミュレータのベイズ推論における勾配情報の活用
papers.summary_ja: 微分方程式ベースの高コストシミュレータを用いたベイズ推論において、ガウス過程サロゲートモデルとベイズ最適化を組み合わせた能動学習手法を提案する。シミュレータ出力の勾配情報をサロゲートモデルに組み込むことで、限られた計算予算下での収束速度を大幅に向上させることを示した。逆モード微分を用いる場合、追加計算コストを考慮しても推論効率の向上が確認された一方、順モード微分ではコストに見合わない結果となった。パラメータ数が出力次元数を超える問題において、勾配強化サロゲートが特に有効であることが判明した。

papers.title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
papers.summary: Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems, from structural buckling to fluid and climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning. At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation, a single input admits multiple equally valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption underlying most learned physical surrogates. We introduce Bi-FORK, a generative framework for learning these one-to-many solution maps in high-dimensional systems. Bi-FORK generates complete trajectories through latent flow matching, preserving space and time coherence, and uses repulsion-guided sampling to recover distinct solution branches in a single amortized pass. We evaluate Bi-FORK on buckling beams, mechanical metamaterials, and Allen-Cahn phase separation, spanning continuous, discrete, and field-valued bifurcations with discretizations up to 260,000 points. Bi-FORK recovers the multimodal solution structure while scaling several orders of magnitude beyond prior approaches, opening generative modeling to high-dimensional bifurcating physical systems.
papers.title_ja: Bi-FORK: 高次元分岐システムの生成モデリング
papers.summary_ja: 対称性の破れによる分岐現象では、単一の入力に対して複数の有効解が存在するため、従来の1対1対応を前提とする物理サロゲートモデルでは扱いにくい。本論文は、潜在空間でのフローマッチングと反発ガイドサンプリングを用いることで、高次元システムにおける1対多の解マッピングを学習する生成フレームワーク「Bi-FORK」を提案する。バール梁の座屈、メカニカルメタマテリアル、Allen-Cahn相分離など、最大26万点の離散化を含む多様な物理システムで評価し、既存手法より桁違いに高い次元数でも多峰な解構造を再現できることを示した。

papers.title: AB-PIELMs: Adaptive-Basis Physics-Informed Extreme Learning Machines for Residual-Driven Domain Decomposition
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural solvers often struggle with multiscale behavior and sharp gradients due to the use of global approximation spaces and nonconvex training. We introduce AB-PIELM, an adaptive-basis physics-informed extreme learning machine that combines domain decomposition with joint optimisation of spatial and spectral hyperparameters while retaining deterministic normal-equation training. The method adapts both the number and placement of subdomains and the locality of radial basis functions, enabling problem-dependent allocation of representational capacity without modifying the underlying solver. Experiments on oscillatory function approximation and singularly perturbed advection-diffusion equations demonstrate accurate solutions across a wide range of stiffness regimes while using substantially fewer neurons than existing neural and PIELM-based approaches. The learned hyperparameters are interpretable, concentrating resolution near sharp gradients. The framework also supports inverse problems, successfully recovering diffusion coefficients from sparse noisy observations using Bayesian optimisation. These results indicate that adaptive-basis PIELM formulations provide an efficient and stable alternative to gradient-trained neural PDE solvers and naturally extend to broader classes of differential equations.
papers.title_ja: AB-PIELMs: 残差駆動型領域分割のための適応基底物理情報極限学習機械
papers.summary_ja: 多スケール挙動や急峻な勾配を持つ物理方程式の解法として、適応基底物理情報極限学習機械（AB-PIELM）を提案する。領域分解と空間・周波数ハイパーパラメータの同時最適化により、解算器を変更せずに表現能力を問題依存型で配分する。振動関数近似や特異摂動拡散方程式において、既存のニューラルソルバーより少ないニューロン数で高精度な解を得ることを示した。さらにベイズ最適化を用いた逆問題への適用も成功し、勾配学習型ソルバーの効率的かつ安定した代替手段となることを実証した。

papers.title: Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning
papers.summary: Planning is increasingly important for long-horizon agents, where successful execution requires coordinating subgoals, tool use, and intermediate outcomes over many steps. Yet assumptions made during planning may be invalidated by the environment, tools may return unexpected results, or actions may fail. Effective agents must therefore not only generate plans, but also revise them. Such revisions often affect only part of a plan, leaving the preceding and subsequent structure intact. Rather than regenerate the entire plan and risk unnecessary changes, repair can regenerate the affected region conditioned on the preserved prefix and suffix. We introduce Plan-and-Patch, a plan-and-act framework in which a diffusion language model (dLLM) generates a structured, program-like plan through parallel unmasking and repairs it by filling in selected regions while keeping the surrounding steps fixed. We compare DreamReasoner-8B and Qwen3-8B as diffusion and autoregressive (AR) planners. On Natural Plan without task-specific training, diffusion (53.7%) achieves nearly twice the plan repair success rate of AR (27.0%). After task-specific training on agentic benchmarks, ALFWorld and TextCraft, the planners achieve similar observed success in plan generation, while diffusion reduces mean plan-generation latency by 39-46% relative to AR. Our results show that Plan-and-Patch provides a framework for faster plan generation and effective plan repair in long-horizon agents.
papers.title_ja: Plan-and-Patch: エージェント型計画のための拡散言語モデル
papers.summary_ja: 長期的なエージェントタスクにおける計画の修正効率を高めるための新フレームワーク「Plan-and-Patch」を提案する。拡散言語モデル（dLLM）を用いることで、計画の一部のみを条件付きで再生成し、前後の構造を維持したまま効率的に修正（パッチ）を行う。自己回帰モデルと比較し、計画修正の成功率が約2倍に向上し、タスク特化学習後は計画生成のレイテンシが39〜46%短縮されることを示した。
